A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. Inspection includes all appendices: A-D in v3 and A-G in v4. Renamed tasks and relocated results can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of five LLMs on three literature-review tasks, disciplinary analyses, and human validation using 100 generated references.

after.justification: v4 retains these original evaluations and adds citation-frequency statistics and correlations with reference precision.

M1.justification: The generation tasks, prompts, reference-validity rule, and NLI/KPR procedures remain unchanged. Task independence, candidate-set merging, and normalization receive additional explanation, without evidence of a changed underlying procedure. Added evaluation metrics are assessed under E3.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same reported 1,105 reviews from 51 Annual Reviews journals published in 2023, with the same disciplinary coverage and three tasks. The CRISPR review example in v4 Appendix F illustrates retained coverage; continuously updated datasets remain a future plan.

E2.justification: The same five models participate in the corresponding comparisons: Qwen-2.5-72B, Llama-3.2-3B, DeepSeek-V3, GPT-4o, and Claude-3.5-Sonnet. TRUE and GPT-4o remain the evaluators. Newly cited CHIME and SurveyX are not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: v4 adds F1 evaluation in Tables 1 and 3, combining the existing accuracy and overlap measurements now labeled precision and recall. The prompts, model versions, reference counts, output lengths, and matching threshold are retained. Temperature zero and official API use are newly disclosed settings, not established changes.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and the new Table 4 examine whether citation popularity accompanies higher reference precision across disciplines, using Claude-3.5-Sonnet and DeepSeek-V3. Existing analyses of publication years, metadata fields, disciplines, and human-reference overlap remain.

E5.justification: v4 adds correlation estimation between average citation counts and disciplinary precision, reporting 0.40 for Claude and 0.51 for DeepSeek. The existing ANOVA tests and p-values are moved to Appendix G unchanged. Human-validation agreement reporting is retained; no repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting expansion is documented.

E6.justification: Shared main performance values are unchanged. v4 adds derived F1 scores, including Claude's 33.08 for Reference Generation and 41.42 for Review Composition, plus citation-count statistics, correlations, and an illustrative generated review. These are additional reported results, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The reference-validity conditions and NLI/KPR equations retain their mathematical substance. Index notation is cleaned up and accuracy is renamed precision. Adding standard harmonic-mean F1 reporting does not introduce new theoretical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: an automated three-task evaluation framework, a multidisciplinary human-review benchmark, persistent reference hallucinations, and disciplinary performance differences. Renaming literature summary as abstract writing clarifies the existing task.

C2.justification: v4 substantially expands applicability and validity qualifications, discussing possible training-data contamination, incomplete Semantic Scholar retrieval, and missing dimensions of review quality. It also interprets citation popularity through possible training-data exposure and explains abstract writing as a proxy for review planning. These extend v3's brief limitations substantially.

D1.justification: v4 newly supplies a repository link with reported code/data availability, specifies official API use and temperature zero, and documents author-name and journal-title normalization in Appendix E. It also explains candidate merging and deduplication, attributes the retained 80% title threshold to human evaluation, and identifies annotators as research-team members. These materially expand reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: v4 adds CHIME by Hsu et al. and SurveyX by Liang et al. to the research context. It also resolves the missing Chelli et al. citation for a study already described in v3. The central positioning around automated, multidisciplinary evaluation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Related work, task descriptions, metric explanations, and main-result prose receive extensive rewriting. Descriptive task names replace numbered labels throughout much of the paper. The standalone overlap subsection is absorbed into the main evaluation presentation, ANOVA details move to Appendix G, and the limitations and appendices are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: The central results display is substantially reorganized: overlap columns from v3 Table 4 enter expanded Tables 1 and 3 alongside F1, and a new citation-frequency table replaces that display. Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 2 changes ticks, markers, and legend presentation, and Figure 4 relabels accuracy as precision while retaining its bars.

improvement.justification: v4 improves transparency through clearer task explanations, normalization and API details, reported code/data access, and explicit contamination and retrieval limitations. The citation-frequency analysis adds limited supporting evidence. However, relabeling v3's generated-reference overlap as recall without clearly specifying its denominator weakens the justification for the new F1 scores. With the core empirical evidence unchanged, the net improvement is useful but limited.
